context:
Goal: a guard's wrong refusals cost less than the harm it stops.
In plain words: the guard reads each shell command before it runs. The 'reader' is the part that splits a command into pieces so the guard can judge them. A 'glued &' is an & typed with no space, like `build&echo done`: the shell runs the left part in the background, so a check could hide behind it. PR #2156 teaches the reader to see that.
Problem (rule): the risk is the reader refusing valid commands, because & also appears inside a web address like `curl x?a=1&b=2`. Wrong refusals on record: that one (with a wrong fix printed), `$[1&2]`, and `ci-job checks --lint & echo $! | cat`. How often it refuses wrongly is unmeasured, so R5's test ('only when its wrong refusals cost more than the harm it stops') cannot be run.
Based on (ruling): R5; decision guard-that-cries-wolf-is-spent.
Departs from: main — main lists the gap as debt check-tail-trailing-amp; keeping adds the reader.

options.how: Close #2156 after the ledger; the gap stays a debt.
options.label: Drop the widening (triage's pick)
options.lose: A trailing & that hides a check is still caught only as a debt.

options.how: Rebuild on #2015 as the lane proposes.
options.label: Keep the widening
options.lose: Wrong refusals with an unmeasured rate.

reply: You asked what 'glued' and 'reader' mean; the item now says it in plain words. Nothing else changed: a drops the glued-& reader, b keeps it.
title: Keep PR #2156's glued-& reader on top of the any-filter, which may refuse valid commands?
